# The framework examples' cases, which scripts/go-examples.sh runs
# (docs/decisions/0014-PLAN-api-policy-gates.md Step 5, deviation D6):
#
#   <framework> <args…> => <exit> stdout|stderr <substring>
#
# The framework is the program's directory. The substring is the rest of the
# line, matched literally in the stream named. A bad flag's exit status is
# each framework's own, as measured: 2 for flag, 80 for kong, 1 for cobra and
# urfave.

flag save notes => 1 stderr refused: session.save
flag save --yes notes => 0 stdout saved notes
flag save --bogus notes => 2 stderr flag provided but not defined: -bogus

cobra save notes => 1 stderr refused: session.save
cobra save --yes notes => 0 stdout saved notes
cobra save --bogus notes => 1 stderr unknown flag: --bogus

kong save notes => 1 stderr refused: session.save
kong save --yes notes => 0 stdout saved notes
kong save --bogus notes => 80 stderr unknown flag --bogus

urfave save notes => 1 stderr refused: session.save
urfave save --yes notes => 0 stdout saved notes
urfave save --bogus notes => 1 stderr flag provided but not defined: -bogus

# The --tui path, with no terminal: a warning naming the reason, then the
# line mode. --mode=plain goes to the line mode with no warning.
flag --tui => 0 stderr launch.input-not-terminal
flag --tui => 0 stdout line mode
flag --mode=plain => 0 stdout line mode
cobra --tui => 0 stderr launch.input-not-terminal
cobra --tui => 0 stdout line mode
cobra --mode=plain => 0 stdout line mode
kong --tui => 0 stderr launch.input-not-terminal
kong --tui => 0 stdout line mode
kong --mode=plain => 0 stdout line mode
urfave --tui => 0 stderr launch.input-not-terminal
urfave --tui => 0 stdout line mode
urfave --mode=plain => 0 stdout line mode
